newsitem.title: UK: Large hole in UK Labour's spending plans - Major.
newsitem.headline: Large hole in UK Labour's spending plans - Major.

text.p: Conservative Prime Minister John Major launched another attack on the spending and tax plans of the Britain's main opposition Labour Party on Friday.
Major said that Labour's chief finance spokesman Gordon Brown had acknowledged a 1.5 billion stg gap between Labour's tax and spending plans on Thursday but said the difference was actually larger.
"In fact the gap is much bigger as Ken Clarke will show later this morning," Major added, speaking on BBC Radio 4.
Conservative finance minister Kenneth Clarke will speak at a press conference today as part of the May 1 election campaign.
Major said that although Labour had pledged not to raise income tax it had not mentioned the 200 other forms of taxation that could be altered.
Major said that the Labour Party were "rather flaky" on the detail of policy.
Labour has a lead of more than 21 points over the Conservatives in the opinion polls.
